samples.ref: We developed a simplified deterministic susceptible-exposed-infectious-removed (SEIR) mathematical model to assess the effect of active isolation of SARS-CoV-2 infected but asymptomatic individuals through blanket testing for control of the outbreak in Lusaka Province of Zambia.

samples.src: Mo re laeditše diponagalo tše pedi; (1) ya go akanya gore batho bao ba sa laetšego maswao ba bopa 70% tša malwetši ka moka a COVID-19 le (2) ya gore batho bao ba sa laetšego maswao ba bopa fela 50% tša malwetši.
samples.ref: Here we modelled two scenarios; (1) assuming asymptomatic individuals comprised 70% of all COVID-19 cases and (2) asymptomatic individuals comprised only 50% of the cases.

samples.ref: For contrast, the model was assessed first under the assumption that asymptomatic individuals are equally as infectious as symptomatic individuals and then secondly, and more likely, assuming asymptomatic individuals are only half as infectious as symptomatic individuals.

samples.src: Go mmotlolo wo o akanyago gore ke 70% tša malwetši ao a sa laetšego maswao, kelo ya fasefase ya diteko tše di ka dirwago tša batho ka bontši tše≥ diteko tše 7911/go batho ba 100000 e be e kgotsofatša go laola go phulega ga bolwetši ge e ba batho bao ba sa laetšego maswao e le seripagare fela sa bao ba ka fetetšegago bolwetši mola e le gore ge go akanywa gore ke phetetšano ya tekatekano, gona kelo ya ≥ diteko tše 10028/go batho ba 100000 e tla hlokega.
samples.ref: For the model assuming 70% asymptomatic cases, a minimum sustained daily blanket testing rate of ≥ 7911 tests/100000 population was sufficient to control the outbreak if asymptomatic individuals are only half as infectious while if equal infectiousness was assumed then a testing rate of ≥ 10028 tests/ 100000 population would be required.

samples.ref: The researchers looked at patient records for 214 women who had been screened and treated for HPV, lesions, and cervical cancer at a hospital in Windhoek, Namibia.
samples.hyp:
Ba ile ba hwetša gore 38.3% ya basadi ba ne ba na le tšhupo ya HPV, 23.4% ba ne ba na le tšhupo ya mabadi, mme 1.9% ba ne ba alafetšwe kankere ya molomo wa popelo. Go tšwa go bona, go lemogile gore go na le tshepo e kgolo ya go alafetšwa ka kankere ya molomo wa popelo mo basadinyana ba ba alafetšwego ka mabadi.

Researchers analyzed the medical records of 214 women who underwent screening for HPV, precancerous lesions, and cervical cancer at a clinic in Windhoek, Namibia. They found that 38.3% of the women had evidence of HPV infection, 23.4% had precancerous lesions, and 1.9% were diagnosed with cervical cancer. Furthermore, it was observed that there is a strong association between the presence of precancerous lesions and the diagnosis of cervical cancer.

samples.ref: A sample of 377 women was surveyed, leading to the findings that women in Shiroro are highly entrepreneurial with high level of financial independence, engaging mostly in SMEs.

samples.src: Metswako ye dingwe ka dinyakišišong e bile motswako wa payotšha ya kompose ya mmutedi wa dikgogo le mekgokgothi ya lefela goba payotšha ya makgapetla a raese (kompose ya 1 % + payotšha ya 1%: mabu a 1% w/w), go lekodišiša diabe tša tšona godimo ga go hema moya ga mabu a pasale, pH ya mabu; kelo ya khapone ya maekhropiale mabung; bogolo bja phetošetšano ya kheišene; kelo ya methopo ya khapone, kelo ya naetrotšene le kelo ya naetrotšene ye e lego gona.
samples.ref: Other treatments in the study were combined poultry manure compost and corn cob biochar or rice husk biochar (1 % compost + 1% biochar: 1% soil w/w), respectively, to examine their effects on basal soil respiration, soil pH; soil microbial carbon; cation exchange capacity; total organic carbon, total nitrogen and available nitrogen concentration.

samples.ref: Biochar and compost applied solely or together, and composted biochar increased soil pH by 0.28–2.29 pH units compared to the un-amended control.

samples.hyp: Go na le mekgwa e e fapanego ya go hlahloba mobu, eupša tsela yeo e tswalegang ke yeo e sebedišago dikarolo tše tsheletswe tša mobu: ditokomanelo, ditiragalo, ditiragalo tša ka kgwedi, ditiragalo tše di tšwago mo lebokong, ditiragalo tša ka ntle, le ditiragalo tša ka ntle.
